about: The contract of the Node rows bridge: the one door the Rust host uses to reach the doctor rows and fixes whose layers Node still owns (owner bridge:<step> in doctor-registry.v1.json). The host starts `module` of the legacy payload with the payload's Node, writes one request as JSON on its stdin and reads one line per result from its stdout. Only a line that starts with resultPrefix is a result, so output a body prints can never be read as one; each result is written as soon as it exists, so a crash keeps what was produced; the call ends with one `end` line carrying the number of results and, optionally, `nodeVersion` (the `process.version` of the Node that ran the call, which the host judges against the release's `requires.node` instead of starting a Node of its own), and a call without it did not finish. A malformed request or an id with no body is one `refusal` line. Three more requests share the door until the Work layer moves. `work-store-init` creates the Work store of the project's `.fgos` (the Event Store rebuild `fgos init` needs); it has no ids, answers with an `end` line of count 0 when it worked, and with a `refusal` line whose optional `category` is the error's exit category when it did not. `work-dispatch-hint` is the Work lookup of `fgos dispatch decide --work <id> [--stage <stage>]`: it has no ids and carries `workId` and an optional `stage`; it answers with one `hint` line (`hint` is the dispatch hint object of the Work item at that stage, or null when the Work store holds no such item) and an `end` line of count 1, and with a `refusal` line when the lookup failed. `work-questions` is the read of what waits for the owner outside the question store (`fgos questions`): it has no ids; it answers with one `data` line (`data` is `{gates, asks}`: the open Workflow gates, each `{ref, question, answerDoor}`, and the `fgos ask` items of the Work view, each `{ref, title, question, answerDoor}`) and an `end` line of count 1, and with a `refusal` line when a read failed. The level of a row (`status` when the row does not say it), the fix of a failing row, `ok` and `next` are the host's, never the bridge's. Each side reads `vectors`: the Node module writes exactly `line` for `kind` and `body`, the host reads `line` back as `body`. The bridge ends with the last Node-owned row.

request.phase: `fix` (every id is a fix id), `check` (every id is a row id), `work-store-init` (no ids), `work-dispatch-hint` (no ids) or `work-questions` (no ids)
request.ids: a non-empty-string id each, in registry order; one call per run of consecutive fixes of the bridge, one call for every bridged row; an empty list for `work-store-init`, `work-dispatch-hint` and `work-questions`
request.dir: the project root the run acts on (for `work-store-init`, the project whose `.fgos` the store is created in; for `work-dispatch-hint` and `work-questions`, the main checkout whose `.fgos` holds the Work store)
request.workId: `work-dispatch-hint` only: the Work item id, a non-empty string
request.stage: `work-dispatch-hint` only: the stage the item is dispatched at; absent when the caller named none

vectors.name: a judged row with everything it can say
a judged row with only a verdict
the dispatch hint of a Work item
the dispatch hint of a Work item the store does not hold
the end of a finished call
the end of a call that reports the Node that ran it
a refusal of the whole call
a refusal of the Work store step, with its category

body.message: lock-timeout: the project lock stayed held

vectors.line: FGOS-DOCTOR-BRIDGE {"kind":"refusal","message":"lock-timeout: the project lock stayed held","category":"lock-timeout"}

vectors.name: the questions the Work layer holds for the owner
